title: Writing up a signal
objectives: Write a research note with IC, turnover and Sharpe after costs.
Run the pipeline end to end and say what changes for real data.

screens.title: Which note gets funded?
screens.prose: The pipeline is built. A research committee now reads two notes on the same momentum study. Tap the one it can fund, or turn down, with confidence.
screens.question: Tap the note the committee can act on.

hints.text: Which note lets a reader check the claim?
Note A gives one gross number and no costs.
Note B shows costs, intervals, the held-out year and $N$.

feedback.correct: Correct. Note B can be checked, even though its news is mixed.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Which note says what the number is after costs, how sure it is, and what was tried?

byKey.left: You picked the confident note. Its 1.82 is gross, with no interval, no $N$ and no held-out year.

explain.text: Note A's 1.82 is the gross research Sharpe: no costs, no interval, no count of tries. Note B is less exciting and far more useful. A committee funds what it can check.

screens.title: The template
screens.prose: The note follows the backtest course's results template, with research headings. One page, ten headings, in the order a reader asks: what was asked, on what data, how measured, how traded, what it cost, what came out, how hard we looked, what failed, what next. The pipeline above feeds it.
screens.question: Put the note's headings in order.

hints.text: Start with the question and the data; finish with what next.
Measurement comes before the portfolio, and costs before results.
Variants tried and What failed come after Results.

feedback.correct: Correct. Those are the headings, in order.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Follow the pipeline: data, signal, measurement, portfolio, costs, then results and honesty.

explain.text: The order follows the pipeline, so each section uses only what came before it. Results come after costs, so a gross number never stands alone. Variants tried and What failed sit next to the result they qualify.

screens.title: Where the numbers come from
screens.prose: The Costs section reports turnover a year, cost a year in bp at the stated book, and the break-even cost per £ traded.
screens.question: Tap the stages that produce the Costs section's numbers.

hints.text: Turnover comes from the weights.
Break-even needs the gross return and the £ traded.
Both come from the portfolio stage, and the cost model adds the rest.

feedback.correct: Correct. Weights and the cost model.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Which stages know the weights and the price of trading?

byKey.ic: The IC measures the signal, not the trading. Turnover comes from the portfolio's weights.
byKey.signal: The signal's speed predicts turnover, but turnover is measured on the weights.
byKey.note: The note only prints the numbers.

explain.text: Turnover and the gross return come from the portfolio; the spreads, volumes and impact come from the cost stage. If a reviewer doubts a cost figure, those two stages are where to look.

screens.title: The Measurement section
screens.prose: `run_research` returns the monthly rank ICs of 12−1 momentum on the research period's rebalance dates. Fill in the two summary numbers the section needs, from lesson 9: the t statistic $\bar{IC}/s \times \sqrt{n}$ and the annual IC information ratio $\bar{IC}/s \times \sqrt{12}$.
screens.question: Fill in the t statistic and the IR to 2 decimal places.

hints.text: Divide the mean by the sd first.
Times √35 = 5.916 for t; times √12 = 3.464 for the IR.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Mean over sd, then times √n or √12.

explain.text: t = 2.30 on 35 non-overlapping months, IR = 1.34, hit rate 63%. The quintile row adds the staircase: 0.22%, 0.81%, 0.75%, 0.83%, 1.52% a month, rising at the ends but not monotone in the middle. Both go in the note, the kink included.

screens.title: The Costs section
screens.prose: At a £100m book the run reports turnover 2.3386 a year and costs 165.4 bp a year, against a gross return of 5.24% a year. Fill in the two numbers a PM reads first.
screens.question: Fill in the break-even cost in bp per £ traded (to 0 places) and the net return a year in % (to 2 places).

hints.text: £ traded a year is twice the turnover.
Net return: gross minus 165.4 bp.

feedback.correct: Correct. The book breaks even far above its real costs.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Divide gross return by both sides of the turnover; subtract the cost for the net.

explain.text: Break-even is 0.0524 / 4.677 = 112 bp per £ traded; the real cost averages about 35 bp. Net return is 5.24% − 1.65% = 3.58% a year. The section also says borrow costs are excluded.

screens.title: The Results section
screens.prose: Research period: gross 1.82, net 1.23 (95% interval 0.10 to 2.35), maximum drawdown −3.6%. Held-out year: net −0.49 (−2.45 to 1.47).
screens.question: Which Results sentence is honest?

options.text: Net Sharpe 1.23 in research (0.10 to 2.35) and −0.49 in the held-out year (−2.45 to 1.47); one year cannot confirm or refute the research figure.
Sharpe 1.82.
options.why: You chose the gross research number alone: no costs, no interval, no held-out year.

options.text: Net Sharpe 1.23 (95% interval 0.10 to 2.35).
options.why: The interval is there, but the held-out year is left out because it was bad.

options.text: The held-out Sharpe of −0.49 proves momentum does not work.
options.why: One year's interval runs from about −2.4 to 1.5. It proves nothing either way.

hints.text: A result needs costs, an interval and the held-out year.
Which option has all three?
And claims no more than one year can show.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Look for net, interval and held-out year together.

byKey.c: You dropped the held-out year. Leaving out the one untouched result is the worst omission a note can make.

explain.text: Option A gives both periods, each with its interval, and claims only what one year can support. The table goes in the note as it stands, beside the maximum drawdown.

screens.title: The What failed section
screens.prose: The rubric for What failed: specific, quantified, names what was tried and dropped, and makes no excuses. Six draft lines from this study.
screens.question: Select all that apply: the lines that meet the rubric.

options.text: Reversal: gross Sharpe 3.42 at daily rebalancing, net −18.8 at £100m; costs of 59% a year ate the edge.
The held-out year's net Sharpe was −0.49 (interval −2.45 to 1.47), against 1.23 in research.
With 37 variants tried, the net Sharpe of 1.23 is below the 1.24 expected from luck: the deflated check failed.
The 50/50 combination: gross Sharpe 2.15 but net 0.00 at £100m; its reversal leg traded 6.1 times a year.
Some things did not work as well as hoped.
options.why: It names nothing and measures nothing. A reader cannot check it.

options.text: Momentum was weaker in 2023 because of market conditions.
options.why: It is an excuse, not a measurement: no number, and a cause nobody tested.

hints.text: Does each line give a number a reader can check?
Two lines have no number at all.
Four lines are specific and measured.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Keep every line that is specific and measured; drop the vague one and the excuse.

explain.text: Each kept line names a thing tried, gives its number, and does not explain it away. The study's best gross numbers both died at £100m, and that is the most useful finding in the note.

screens.title: Nothing failed
screens.prose: A colleague's note is complete except one section. It reads: "What failed: nothing major. The momentum signal performed as expected." Its Results section shows only the research period.

lines: Nothing major. The momentum signal performed as expected.
params.title: Draft

screens.question: What should the reviewer ask for?

options.text: The held-out year's result, and the measured failures: the dropped variants and the deflated check
Nothing: if nothing failed, the section can say so
options.why: Thirty-seven variants were tried and most were dropped. Something failed, every time.

options.text: A longer explanation of why the signal works
options.why: That adds a story, not evidence. The missing pieces are the held-out year and the failures.

options.text: A higher Sharpe before the note goes out
options.why: Tuning until the number looks good is exactly what the trial count guards against.

hints.text: Which result is missing from Results?
And what happened to the variants that were dropped?
A real study always has failures to report.

feedback.correct: Correct. An empty What failed means the search is hidden.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Ask what the draft leaves out.

byKey.b: You accepted "nothing". A study that tried 37 variants and kept one has 36 stories to tell.

explain.text: "Nothing failed" hides the search, and research-only results hide the test. Our `research_note` refuses an empty list, so the gap cannot reach a reader.

screens.title: The note and the repository
screens.prose:
The rule, as the code writes it:

```text
# Research note
## Question       ## Data        ## Signals
## Measurement    ## Portfolio   ## Costs
## Results        ## Variants tried
## What failed    ## Next steps
```

Results carry $SR_{\text{net}} \pm 1.96\,SE$ for both periods, and Variants tried compares it with $E[\max_N]$. Beside the note the repository has a README (what it does, how to run it, how to run the tests) and the tests that ran: the look-ahead spies and the alignment tests.
screens.question: Which belongs in the Data section?

options.text: The universe rule, how splits, dividends and dead shares were handled, and the dates of each period
The mean IC and its t statistic
options.why: Those measure the signal: they go under Measurement.

options.text: The net Sharpe and its interval
options.why: That is the outcome: it goes under Results.

options.text: The number of variants tried
options.why: That has its own heading, Variants tried, next to the result it qualifies.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Data says what went in, not what came out.

explain.text: Data is everything a reader needs to rebuild the panel: source, seed or vendor, dates, the point-in-time universe, adjustments and the handling of delisted shares. Levels 1 to 3 of this course each wrote one of those sentences.

screens.title: The study, end to end
screens.prose: Every earlier piece is defined, and `P = make_panel()` is built: seed 2310, 200 shares, 1,260 days. `run_research` assembles them; fill the four gaps. The universe applies to the signal; the IC uses only rebalance dates whose forward window ends before the held-out year; costs land the day after each rebalance.
screens.question: Fill the four gaps in `run_research(p, config)`.

widget.prelude:
import math
from statistics import NormalDist
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def make_panel(n_stocks=200, n_days=1260, seed=2310):
    """Seeded stand-in for a few years of daily data on a share universe."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    names = [f"S{i:03d}" for i in range(n_stocks)]
    dates = pd.bdate_range("2019-01-02", periods=n_days)
    sector = rng.integers(0, 5, n_stocks)
    beta = 0.6 + 0.8 * rng.random(n_stocks)
    mkt = 0.0003 + 0.010 * rng.standard_normal(n_days)
    sec = 0.005 * rng.standard_normal((n_days, 5))
    z_mu = rng.standard_normal((n_days, n_stocks))
    z_tr = rng.standard_normal((n_days, n_stocks))
    idio = 0.015 * rng.standard_normal((n_days, n_stocks))
    mu = np.zeros(n_stocks); u = np.zeros(n_stocks)
    ret = np.empty((n_days, n_stocks))
    k = 0.0004 * np.sqrt(1 - 0.995 ** 2)
    for t in range(n_days):
        mu = 0.995 * mu + k * z_mu[t]              # slow drift: momentum
        u_new = 0.8 * u + 0.006 * z_tr[t]          # transient part: reversal
        ret[t] = beta * mkt[t] + sec[t, sector] + mu + idio[t] + (u_new - u)
        u = u_new
    # listings and delistings: 10% list late, 10% die (last day -50% to -100%)
    listed = np.ones((n_days, n_stocks), bool)
    late = rng.choice(n_stocks, n_stocks // 10, replace=False)
    for j in late:
        listed[: rng.integers(60, n_days // 2), j] = False
    dead = rng.choice(np.setdiff1d(np.arange(n_stocks), late), n_stocks // 10, replace=False)
    for j in dead:
        d = rng.integers(n_days // 4, n_days - 20)
        ret[d, j] = np.log(1 - rng.uniform(0.5, 1.0) + 1e-4)
        listed[d + 1 :, j] = False
    ret = np.where(listed, ret, np.nan)
    simple = np.expm1(ret)
    # dividends: half the shares pay 0.5% a quarter; splits: 15 two-for-one
    div_yield = np.zeros((n_days, n_stocks))
    payers = rng.random(n_stocks) < 0.5
    div_yield[63::63, :] = np.where(payers, 0.005, 0.0)
    split = np.ones((n_days, n_stocks))
    for j in rng.choice(n_stocks, 15, replace=False):
        split[rng.integers(100, n_days - 100), j] = 2.0
    price_ret = (1 + np.nan_to_num(simple)) / (1 + div_yield) - 1
    start = rng.uniform(20, 200, n_stocks)
    adj_close = start * np.cumprod(1 + price_ret, axis=0)    # split-adjusted, no dividends
    later = np.cumprod(split[::-1], axis=0)[::-1]              # splits on or after each day
    raw_close = adj_close * np.vstack([later[1:], np.ones(n_stocks)])
    # spreads and volume: bigger names are cheaper to trade
    size = rng.lognormal(0, 1, n_stocks)
    half_spread_bp = np.clip(8 / np.sqrt(size), 1, 30)
    adv_gbp = 2e7 * size
    F = lambda a: pd.DataFrame(a, index=dates, columns=names)
    return {"ret": F(simple), "raw_close": F(np.where(listed, raw_close, np.nan)),
            "adj_close": F(np.where(listed, adj_close, np.nan)),
            "dividend": F(np.where(listed, div_yield * raw_close, 0.0)),
            "split": F(split), "listed": F(listed),
            "sector": pd.Series(sector, index=names), "beta": pd.Series(beta, index=names),
            "half_spread_bp": pd.Series(half_spread_bp, index=names),
            "adv_gbp": pd.Series(adv_gbp, index=names)}

def daily_volume_gbp(p):
    """Each day's £ volume: p["volume_gbp"] if the panel has one, else adv_gbp on every listed day."""
    vol = p["volume_gbp"] if "volume_gbp" in p else p["listed"] * p["adv_gbp"]
    return vol.where(p["listed"])

def universe_mask(p, min_adv_gbp=5e6, window=60):
    adv = daily_volume_gbp(p).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    return p["listed"] & (adv >= min_adv_gbp)

def forward_returns(ret, h):
    if h < 1:
        raise ValueError("a forward return starts the day after: h must be at least 1")
    growth = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    seen = pd.DataFrame(False, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    for k in range(1, h + 1):
        r = ret.shift(-k)                 # the return k days after each row
        growth = growth * (1 + r.fillna(0.0))
        seen = seen | r.notna()
    fwd = (growth - 1).where(seen)
    fwd.iloc[max(len(ret) - h, 0):] = np.nan   # the window runs past the data
    return fwd

def momentum_12_1(ret, lookback=252, skip=21, min_periods=200):
    logret = np.log1p(ret)
    window = lookback - skip          # 231 days: t-251 .. t-21
    total = logret.rolling(window, min_periods=min_periods).sum()
    mom = total.shift(skip)           # row t now ends at t - skip
    return mom.where(ret.notna())     # no signal for a share not listed today

def reversal_5d(ret):
    logret = np.log1p(ret)
    past5 = logret.rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
    return -past5

def cs_zscore(signal, clip=3.0):
    mean = signal.mean(axis=1)              # across shares, NaN skipped
    sd = signal.std(axis=1, ddof=1)         # NaN with one share
    sd = sd.where(sd > 0)                   # all equal: undefined, not infinite
    z = signal.sub(mean, axis=0).div(sd, axis=0)
    return z.clip(-clip, clip)

def combine(signals, weights):
    total = None
    for s, w in zip(signals, weights):
        z = cs_zscore(s) * w
        total = z if total is None else total + z
    return total

def rank_ic(signal, fwd, min_n=10):
    m = signal.notna() & fwd.notna()
    n = m.sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    A = signal.where(m).rank(axis=1).to_numpy(float)
    B = fwd.where(m).rank(axis=1).to_numpy(float)
    k = np.where(n > 0, n, 1)[:, None]
    A = A - np.nansum(A, axis=1, keepdims=True) / k
    B = B - np.nansum(B, axis=1, keepdims=True) / k
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        c = np.nansum(A * B, axis=1) / np.sqrt(np.nansum(A * A, axis=1) * np.nansum(B * B, axis=1))
    c[n < min_n] = np.nan
    return pd.Series(c, index=signal.index).dropna()

def ic_summary(ic, periods_per_year):
    ic = pd.Series(ic, dtype=float).dropna()
    n = len(ic)
    m, s = float(ic.mean()), float(ic.std(ddof=1))
    return {"mean": round(m, 4), "sd": round(s, 4),
            "ir": round(m / s * math.sqrt(periods_per_year), 4),
            "t": round(m / s * math.sqrt(n), 4), "n": n,
            "hit": round(float((ic > 0).mean()), 4)}

def quantile_returns(signal, fwd, q=5):
    m = signal.notna() & fwd.notna()
    r = signal.where(m).rank(axis=1, method="first")
    n = m.sum(axis=1)
    b = np.floor((r - 1).mul(q).div(n, axis=0)) + 1
    out = pd.DataFrame({k: fwd.where(b == k).mean(axis=1) for k in range(1, q + 1)})
    return out[n >= q]

def rebalance_dates(index, rebalance="M"):
    """The last day of each day ("D"), week ("W") or month ("M") in the index."""
    if rebalance == "D":
        return index
    per = index.to_period(rebalance)
    last = np.append(per[:-1] != per[1:], True)
    return index[last]

def long_short_weights(signal, min_names=10):
    r = signal.rank(axis=1)
    d = r.sub(r.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    gross = d.abs().sum(axis=1)
    n = signal.notna().sum(axis=1)
    w = d.div(gross.where((gross > 0) & (n >= min_names)), axis=0)
    return w.fillna(0.0)

def portfolio_returns(weights, ret, rebalance="M"):
    dates = rebalance_dates(weights.index, rebalance)
    held = weights.loc[dates].reindex(weights.index).ffill().shift(1)
    r = ret.reindex(index=weights.index, columns=weights.columns).fillna(0.0)
    out = (held.fillna(0.0) * r).sum(axis=1)
    live = held.abs().sum(axis=1) > 0
    if not live.any():
        return out.iloc[0:0]
    return out.loc[live.idxmax():]

def turnover(weights):
    w = weights.fillna(0.0)
    return 0.5 * (w - w.shift(1).fillna(0.0)).abs().sum(axis=1)

def trade_costs(weights, half_spread_bp, adv_gbp, sigma, book_gbp, c=1.0):
    w = weights.fillna(0.0)
    dw = (w - w.shift(1).fillna(0.0)).abs()
    impact = c * (dw * book_gbp).div(adv_gbp).pow(0.5).mul(sigma)
    rate = impact.add(half_spread_bp / 1e4)
    return (dw * rate).sum(axis=1)

def charge_next_day(cost, index):
    """Spread a cost per rebalance date onto the next day of the index."""
    out = pd.Series(0.0, index=index)
    pos = index.get_indexer(cost.index) + 1
    ok = pos < len(index)
    out.iloc[pos[ok]] = cost.to_numpy()[ok]
    return out

def sharpe(returns, periods):
    x = pd.Series(returns, dtype=float).dropna()
    if len(x) < 2:
        return 0.0
    s = x.std(ddof=1)
    if not s > 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(math.sqrt(periods) * x.mean() / s)

def sharpe_ci(returns, periods, level=0.95):
    x = pd.Series(returns, dtype=float).dropna()
    n = len(x)
    sr = sharpe(x, periods)
    per = sr / math.sqrt(periods)                       # Sharpe per period
    se = math.sqrt((1 + per ** 2 / 2) / n) * math.sqrt(periods)
    z = NormalDist().inv_cdf(0.5 + level / 2)
    return (round(sr, 4), round(sr - z * se, 4), round(sr + z * se, 4))

def max_drawdown(returns):
    wealth = (1 + pd.Series(returns, dtype=float).dropna()).cumprod()
    return float((wealth / wealth.cummax() - 1).min())


P = make_panel()

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def run_research(p, config):
    ret, idx = p["ret"], p["ret"].index
    reb = config.get("rebalance", "M")
    h = {"D": 1, "W": 5, "M": 21}[reb]
    ppy = {"D": 252, "W": 52, "M": 12}[reb]
    if config["signal"] == "momentum":
        sig = momentum_12_1(ret)
    elif config["signal"] == "reversal":
        sig = reversal_5d(ret)
    else:
        a = config.get("weight", 0.5)
        sig = combine([momentum_12_1(ret), reversal_5d(ret)], [a, 1 - a])
    sig = ...                                            # gap 1: point-in-time universe
    cut = len(idx) - config.get("holdout", 252)          # first held-out row
    dates = rebalance_dates(idx, reb)

    # Measurement: rebalance dates whose forward window ends in research
    fwd = forward_returns(ret, h)
    md = ...                                             # gap 2: forward window inside research
    ic = rank_ic(sig.loc[md], fwd.loc[md])
    qr = quantile_returns(sig.loc[md], fwd.loc[md]).mean()

    # Portfolio and costs
    w = long_short_weights(sig)
    gross = portfolio_returns(w, ret, reb)
    wr = w.loc[dates]
    sigma = ret.rolling(60, min_periods=20).std().ffill()
    cost = trade_costs(wr, p["half_spread_bp"], p["adv_gbp"], sigma.loc[dates],
                       config.get("book_gbp", 1e8))
    net = ...                                            # gap 3: costs on the next day

    res, held = gross.index < idx[cut], gross.index >= idx[cut]
    years = res.sum() / 252
    to = turnover(wr).loc[: idx[cut - 1]]
    traded = 2 * to.sum() / years                        # £ traded a year per £ of book
    return {
        "ic": ic_summary(ic, ppy),
        "quintiles": [round(float(v), 4) for v in qr],
        "turnover": round(float(to.sum() / years), 4),
        "cost_bp": round(float(cost.loc[: idx[cut - 1]].sum() / years * 1e4), 1),
        "break_even_bp": round(float(gross[res].mean() * 252 / traded * 1e4), 1),
        "sharpe_gross": round(sharpe(gross[res], 252), 4),
        "sharpe_net": round(sharpe(net[res], 252), 4),
        "ci": ...,                                       # gap 4: (lo, hi) of the net Sharpe
        "max_drawdown": round(max_drawdown(net[res]), 4),
        "n_obs": int(res.sum()),
        "held_out": {"sharpe_net": round(sharpe(net[held], 252), 4),
                     "ci": sharpe_ci(net[held], 252)[1:], "n_obs": int(held.sum())},
    }

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def run_research(p, config):
    ret, idx = p["ret"], p["ret"].index
    reb = config.get("rebalance", "M")
    h = {"D": 1, "W": 5, "M": 21}[reb]
    ppy = {"D": 252, "W": 52, "M": 12}[reb]
    if config["signal"] == "momentum":
        sig = momentum_12_1(ret)
    elif config["signal"] == "reversal":
        sig = reversal_5d(ret)
    else:
        a = config.get("weight", 0.5)
        sig = combine([momentum_12_1(ret), reversal_5d(ret)], [a, 1 - a])
    sig = sig.where(universe_mask(p))                    # gap 1: point-in-time universe
    cut = len(idx) - config.get("holdout", 252)          # first held-out row
    dates = rebalance_dates(idx, reb)

    # Measurement: rebalance dates whose forward window ends in research
    fwd = forward_returns(ret, h)
    md = dates[dates <= idx[cut - 1 - h]]                # gap 2
    ic = rank_ic(sig.loc[md], fwd.loc[md])
    qr = quantile_returns(sig.loc[md], fwd.loc[md]).mean()

    # Portfolio and costs
    w = long_short_weights(sig)
    gross = portfolio_returns(w, ret, reb)
    wr = w.loc[dates]
    sigma = ret.rolling(60, min_periods=20).std().ffill()
    cost = trade_costs(wr, p["half_spread_bp"], p["adv_gbp"], sigma.loc[dates],
                       config.get("book_gbp", 1e8))
    net = gross - charge_next_day(cost, idx).reindex(gross.index)   # gap 3

    res, held = gross.index < idx[cut], gross.index >= idx[cut]
    years = res.sum() / 252
    to = turnover(wr).loc[: idx[cut - 1]]
    traded = 2 * to.sum() / years                        # £ traded a year per £ of book
    return {
        "ic": ic_summary(ic, ppy),
        "quintiles": [round(float(v), 4) for v in qr],
        "turnover": round(float(to.sum() / years), 4),
        "cost_bp": round(float(cost.loc[: idx[cut - 1]].sum() / years * 1e4), 1),

widget.solution:
import math

HEADINGS = ["Question", "Data", "Signals", "Measurement", "Portfolio", "Costs",
            "Results", "Variants tried", "What failed", "Next steps"]

def research_note(results, n_variants, failures):
    if not failures:
        raise ValueError("a research note must say what failed")
    r, ic, ho = results, results["ic"], results["held_out"]
    sd0 = math.sqrt(252 / (r["n_obs"] - 1))              # Sharpe spread under no skill
    emax, passes = deflated_sharpe_check(r["sharpe_net"], n_variants, sd0, r["n_obs"])
    body = {
        "Question": r.get("question", "Does the signal predict next month's returns across shares, after costs?"),
        "Data": r.get("data", "Seeded make_panel (seed 2310): 200 shares, 1,260 days."),
        "Signals": r.get("signals", "12-minus-1 momentum, ranked across shares on each date."),
        "Measurement": f"Mean IC {ic['mean']:.4f} (t {ic['t']:.2f}, hit rate {ic['hit']:.0%}, {ic['n']} dates).",
        "Portfolio": r.get("portfolio", "Rank weights, longs +0.5 and shorts -0.5, rebalanced monthly, £100m gross."),
        "Costs": f"Turnover {r['turnover']:.2f} a year. Costs {r['cost_bp']:.0f} bp a year. "
                 f"Break-even {r['break_even_bp']:.0f} bp per £ traded.",
        "Results": f"Research: Sharpe gross {r['sharpe_gross']:.2f}, net {r['sharpe_net']:.2f} "
                   f"(95% interval {r['ci'][0]:.2f} to {r['ci'][1]:.2f}). "
                   f"Held-out year: net {ho['sharpe_net']:.2f} "
                   f"(95% interval {ho['ci'][0]:.2f} to {ho['ci'][1]:.2f}). "
                   f"Maximum drawdown {r['max_drawdown']:.1%}.",
        "Variants tried": f"{n_variants} variants tried. Expected best net Sharpe under no skill: "
                          f"{emax:.2f}. Deflated check: {'passed' if passes else 'failed'}.",
        "What failed": "\n".join("- " + f for f in failures),
        "Next steps": r.get("next", "Run the same code on real data with a point-in-time universe."),
    }
    lines = ["# Research note"]
    for h in HEADINGS:
        lines += ["", "## " + h, body[h]]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

byKey.b: Free data handles adjustments. Its gap is the shares that no longer trade.

explain.text: yfinance has only current tickers, so a study on it is survivors only, the bias of lesson 3. Say so in the Data section, or pay for delisted names. yfinance also breaks and rate-limits often: cache every download.

ideas: The note has ten headings in pipeline order, from Question to Next steps, and is generated from the run.
Results give net Sharpe with intervals for research and held-out periods; Variants tried gives $N$ and the deflated check.
What failed is compulsory, specific and measured; on real data the hard part is a point-in-time universe with delisted shares.
